statement: In unrestricted iid FPP on Z^2 with edge weights uniform on {1,2}, T((0,0),(1,1))=min(A1+B1,A2+B2), where A1,A2 are the weights to the two common neighbors and B1,B2 the weights from them to the target. For L=min(A1,A2)+min(B1,B2), P(T>L)=1/8, E(T-L)=1/8, Var(T)=23/64, Var(L)=3/8 and Cov(L,T-L)=-1/16. Independence of the two edge collections does not justify scalar block composition or independence of the matching penalty.
assumptions: Nearest-neighbor undirected FPP on the full Z^2 lattice
proof: Every alternative simple path has at least four edges and cost at least 4; the two length-two paths cost at most 4. Enumerating the sixteen independent assignments yields the stated law and moments. The penalty is one only on (1,2,2,1) and (2,1,1,2).
counterexample: Scalar block minima choose incompatible intermediate vertices in two of sixteen assignments.

statement: For square-integrable T_n=L_n+G_n, if ||G_n-EG_n||_2=o(n^(1/3)) and c*n^(2/3)<=Var(L_n)<=C*n^(2/3) for fixed 0<c<=C and all sufficiently large n, then Var(T_n)/Var(L_n)->1; in particular log Var(T_n)/(2 log n)->1/3.
assumptions: Square-integrable real random variables T_n,L_n,G_n on a common probability space for each n

source.basis: L2 reverse triangle inequality; independently derived conditional lemma, not a solution of P0104.

proof: Apply the reverse triangle inequality to centered variables: |sd(T_n)-sd(L_n)|<=sd(G_n). Divide by sd(L_n)>=sqrt(c)*n^(1/3). The ratio of standard deviations tends to one, and squaring gives the variance ratio.

statement: For nearest-neighbor FPP on Z^d with every edge weight in {1,2}, let T_e(1) and T_e(2) be the passage times between fixed distinct vertices after forcing edge e to weight 1 or 2, with all other weights held fixed. Then T_e(2)-T_e(1)=1 if and only if every minimizing path in the forced-low environment uses e; otherwise the difference is zero. Membership in one arbitrarily selected geodesic is insufficient.
assumptions: All weights take integer values 1 or 2
All other edge weights held fixed under the two forcings
A minimizing path means any path attaining passage time, not a selected tie representative

source.basis: Independent min-plus single-edge proof below; consistent with the intersection-of-all-geodesics convention at equation (5) of https://arxiv.org/pdf/2302.11367; 64 forcing checks in measurements/exact_boundary_counterexample.json.

proof: Positive lower weight and a deterministic Manhattan route bound reduce optimal paths to a finite set. Let A be the minimum cost excluding e among simple paths using e, and B the minimum cost of a path avoiding e, with infinity allowed when a class is empty. Both are integer-valued when finite and T_e(a)=min(A+a,B). The difference is one exactly when A+1<B, equivalent to every forced-low minimizer using e; otherwise an avoiding minimizer persists and the difference is zero. In the all-one four-edge square, any selected geodesic has two edges while all four single-edge increments vanish.
counterexample: All four square weights equal 1: a chosen geodesic contains two edges, neither of which has positive single-edge increment.
